helpGoalText: Find matching emotion pairs! Match faces to the correct words or scenarios.
helpRule1: Click on a card to flip it
helpRule3: If they match, they stay open
helpEasy: Easy: 4 basic emotions (happy, sad, angry, scared)
emotionHappyDesc: When we smile and feel good
emotionSadDesc: When we want to cry and feel down
emotionAngryDesc: When something bothers us and we want to be loud
emotionScaredDesc: When we feel unsafe or afraid
emotionExcitedDesc: When we look forward to something and feel energetic
emotionTiredDesc: When we need rest and feel sleepy
emotionCalmDesc: When we feel relaxed and peaceful
whyEmotionalIntelligenceText: Emotional intelligence is a key life skill. Children who can recognize and name their emotions find it easier to:
supportValidate: Validate feelings: Don't say "That's not a big deal," but "I see you're sad. That's okay."
supportModel: Be a role model: Talk about your own feelings: "I'm frustrated right now because..."
supportPractice: Practice together: Play this game regularly and talk about the scenarios.
supportDaily: Apply daily: Ask: "How do you feel right now?" and help with naming.
supportStories: Use stories: Read our stories and talk about the characters' feelings.
approachText: This game is based on scientific insights from developmental psychology:
approachAge: Age-appropriate: 10 basic emotions that 3-7-year-olds can understand
approachContext: Contextualized: Emotions are shown in real-world situations
approachPositive: Positive reinforcement: Explanations and encouragement after each answer
resourcesText: After the game, you can with your child:
resourcesStories: Read our stories that address emotional topics
resourcesCheck: Build an "emotion check" into daily routine
resourcesRoleplay: Play role-play games with different emotions
noProgressYet: Play your first game to see your progress!
